newsitem.title: USA: PanCanadian to buy CS Resources for C$465 million.
newsitem.headline: PanCanadian to buy CS Resources for C$465 million.

text.p: PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd said Wednesday it agreed to acquire CS Resources Ltd for a total of $521 million ($376 million), including debt.

The deal, under which PanCanadian will pay C$16 per share, or C$465 million ($335 million) in cash and assume C$56 million ($40 million) of CS Resources debt, has been approved by the boards of directors of both companies, it said.
CS Resources' stock closed at C$14.95 Tuesday on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
"This acquisition will combine the strengths of two of Canada's leading heavy oil producers," PanCanadian President and Chief Executive David Tuer said.

"We believe that PanCanadian's offer price will be highly attractive to our shareholders and is certainly a fair price,'' CS Resources Chairman and Chief Executive Dennis Sharp said in a joint statement.

As part of the agreement, CS Resources will pay PanCanadian a non-completion fee of 3 percent in certain circumstances. In addition, CS Resources has granted PanCanadian the right of first refusal to match any subsequent bids. CS Resources has also agreed not to solicit other transaction proposals, it said.

The offer represents a 41.6 percent premium over the closing price of CS Resources' shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange on June 5, the day before Gulf Canada Resources Ltd announced that it planned to bid for CS Resources, the companies said.
The PanCanadian offer is also a 17 percent premium over the value of Gulf Canada's cash and share offer based on Gulf's closing price on June 17, they said.
The offer is conditional upon 66-2/3 percent of CS Resources' outstanding shares being tendered.
PanCanadian, which does not currently own any CS Resources shares, said it will pay for the purchase from existing cash balances.
CS Resources has reported proved and one-half probable crude oil reserves of 132 million barrels and 44 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
Based on first-quarter reports, the combined daily production of the new PanCanadian would be about 155,000 barrels of oil and liquids and 738 million cubic feet of natural gas, the company said.
